title: MPPSC 2026: Mains 7 Sep, Admit Card & Negative Marking
meta_description: MPPSC Mains 7-12 September 2026, admit card from late August at mppsc.mp.gov.in. Prelims result out 22 May, 155 posts, new 3-mark negative marking explained.

hero.one_liner: Madhya Pradesh's state civil services exam - gateway to DSP, Naib Tehsildar, BDO, and Group A/B administrative positions.

what_is_it: MPPSC (Madhya Pradesh Public Service Commission) State Services Examination (SSE) recruits officers for Madhya Pradesh administrative posts: Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP), Naib Tehsildar (revenue), Block Development Officer (BDO), Assistant Director (various departments). Three stages: Prelims (Paper 1: GS 100 Qs, Paper 2: CSAT 100 Qs qualifying), Mains (6 papers totaling 1400 marks), and Interview. MPPSC notification released December 31, 2025, with 155 vacancies for various positions.

MPPSC 2026 Prelims is on April 26, 2026, with application window January 10-February 9, 2026. Notably, MPPSC changed exam pattern: Each question now carries 3 marks (earlier: 1 mark), and negative marking introduced (1 mark per wrong answer). This changes strategy significantly - careless errors are costlier. Mains is scheduled September 7-12, 2026. MP-specific content (20-30% of Prelims GS) tests: MP history (tribal movements, princely states), geography (Narmada, rivers), economy (soybean, agriculture), and current state affairs.

DSP posts at Level 10 (₹56,100 basic) offer ₹80,000-1,00,000/month with DA/allowances. Naib Tehsildar at Level 8 (₹47,600) offers ₹55,000-70,000/month. BDO positions offer similar salary at Level 8-10. MPPSC is moderately easier than UPSC but more difficult than some state PSCs due to increased competition and MP-specific content requirement. Successful candidates prepare 8-12 months with balanced focus on national GS and MP GK.

MPPSC applicants: 4+ lakh for 155-500 vacancies (0.05-0.1% selection rate). Bhopal and Indore are coaching hubs. Unlike UPSC which many reject candidates also attempt, MPPSC attracts serious state-focused aspirants. Advantage: Fewer UPSC toppers compete here, making it relatively more achievable. Disadvantage: MP-specific content cannot be ignored.

extra_sections.heading: Mains Admit Card: What to Check the Day It Drops
content: Log in at mppsc.mp.gov.in with your registration number and date of birth or password. The commission usually opens the download about two weeks before the exam, which puts it in the final week of August.
Check the paper-wise date and shift timing first, since six papers over six days means six separate reporting slots rather than one.
Verify your name spelling, photograph and signature against your application. Discrepancies must be reported to the commission immediately rather than sorted at the centre.
Note the centre address and plan the travel before the first paper. Candidates writing all six papers often book accommodation near the centre for the week.
Carry a printed copy plus a valid photo ID to every paper. No admit card means no entry, and that applies on each of the six days separately.
If the portal does not show your admit card within a couple of days of release, contact the commission rather than waiting. Technical holds are usually fixable, but only before the exam week.

extra_sections.heading: Why MPPSC is among India's most important state PSC exams
content: MPPSC (Madhya Pradesh Public Service Commission) conducts the State Service Examination for recruiting officers to MP Administrative Service, MP Police Service, MP Finance Service, and 20+ allied state services. Madhya Pradesh is India's second-largest state by area and fifth-largest by population, with a diverse geography spanning the Vindhya-Satpura ranges, Narmada valley, Malwa plateau, and Bundelkhand region.
MPPSC attracts 4-6 lakh applicants for 200-500 posts per cycle. The competition is intense but structured - the exam has a well-defined syllabus with heavy emphasis on MP-specific content.

Candidates from MP who invest time in state GK have a significant natural advantage over those who prepare only for general UPSC-style content. MP's governance challenges make MPPSC postings highly impactful.

The state has 21% tribal population (among the highest in India), significant forest cover requiring conservation management, ongoing Naxal presence in some southern districts, and rapid urbanization in cities like Indore, Bhopal, and Jabalpur creating planning challenges. As an MPPSC officer, you directly address these issues.

extra_sections.heading: Exam pattern - Prelims, Mains, Interview
content: Prelims has 2 papers: Paper 1 (General Studies - 100 MCQs, 200 marks, 2 hours) and Paper 2 (General Aptitude Test - 100 MCQs, 200 marks, 2 hours). Both papers count for Prelims merit - unlike UPSC where CSAT is only qualifying.

This makes MPPSC Prelims unique - you must score well in BOTH papers, not just GS. Paper 1 covers: Indian History (ancient, medieval, modern, freedom movement), Indian Geography, MP Geography, Indian Polity, Indian Economy, MP Economy, General Science, Environment, Current Affairs, and MP-specific GK (history, geography, art, culture, tribal affairs).

MP-specific questions carry 35-45% weightage - the single biggest scoring block. Paper 2 covers: Comprehension, communication skills, logical reasoning, analytical ability, decision-making, general mental ability, basic numeracy (Class 10 level), Hindi language comprehension, and data interpretation.
This paper tests aptitude - not subject knowledge. Practice-based preparation with RS Aggarwal Reasoning and basic math works well.

Mains has 6 papers: GS Paper 1 (Indian Heritage, History, Geography - 300 marks), GS Paper 2 (Governance, Constitution, Social Justice - 300 marks), GS Paper 3 (Technology, Economic Development, Environment - 300 marks), GS Paper 4 (Ethics, Integrity, Aptitude - 200 marks), Hindi Language (200 marks - qualifying for non-Hindi medium candidates), and Hindi Essay (100 marks). Interview carries 175 marks.
Total merit: 1,275 marks (Mains) + 175 marks (Interview) = 1,450 marks.

extra_sections.heading: Prelims strategy under the new 3-mark pattern
content: Paper 1 now gives 3 marks for a correct answer and deducts 1 mark for a wrong one. That penalty changes how you should attempt the paper.
Attempt only the questions where you are genuinely confident. Blind guessing now costs you, so leave a question rather than gamble.
Paper 1 (GS) is what shortlists you, so MP GK and current affairs deserve the bulk of your effort. Paper 2 (CSAT) is only qualifying, needing roughly 33%.
Give CSAT enough practice to clear the bar comfortably and no more. The real differentiation happens in Paper 1.

One structural note for this cycle: the topic Life Style and Counter Force was dropped from the Paper 2 syllabus. Older study material still carries it, so skip that section if your book predates 2026.

extra_sections.heading: Paper 2 (CSAT) is qualifying - still clear it
extra_sections.content: Paper 2 does not add to your rank, but you must still clear its cutoff (around 33%). Candidates do fail by ignoring it, so practise enough to cross the bar without stress.

extra_sections.heading: MPPSC Mains structure - six papers, no optional
content: The Mains is fully descriptive and is where your rank is actually built. There are six papers and no optional subject, so every candidate writes the same exam.
Four of them are General Studies papers, GS I to GS IV. Between them they cover history and culture, geography and resources, polity and economy, and science, ethics and general aptitude.
There is also a General Hindi paper and a Hindi Essay paper. The General Hindi paper is qualifying in nature, while the essay and the four GS papers carry the merit marks.
Sources differ a little on the exact totals, with the merit marks usually put at around 1400. Treat the precise split as indicative and confirm it from the official notification at mppsc.mp.gov.in.

Answer-writing practice matters more here than passive reading. Start writing structured answers and one essay a week from the early months, because Mains rewards clarity and speed under time pressure.

GS IV pairs ethics and aptitude with science, and many candidates find it scoring with steady practice. The qualifying General Hindi paper trips up those weak in formal Hindi, so do not leave it to the final week.
Negative marking applies only to Prelims Paper 1. Mains is descriptive throughout, so there is no penalty for attempting a question you are unsure about.

items.title: MP History & culture (15-20% of GS)
items.sub: Bhimbetka rock art and Sanchi Stupa, Paramara and Chandela dynasties, Khajuraho temples, tribal uprisings, 1857 (Tantya Tope, Rani Durgavati). MP formed 1956; Chhattisgarh split off in 2000. See CGPSC for the Chhattisgarh side.

items.title: MP Geography (15-20%)
items.sub: Narmada valley, Malwa Plateau and black cotton soil, major dams (Sardar Sarovar, Bargi, Tawa), tiger reserves (Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Panna), and Panna's diamond mine.

items.title: MP Economy & current affairs
items.sub: MP grows about 60% of India's soybean and is a top wheat and gram producer. Cement, power and tourism matter too. Track state schemes like Ladli Behna, Sikho Kamao and Ladli Laxmi.

extra_sections.heading: Post-selection - MPPSC officer life in MP
content: Starting pay is Pay Level 10 with a basic of ₹56,100. With DA, HRA and state allowances, entry in-hand is roughly ₹75,000 to ₹95,000 a month depending on city.

Government vehicle, residential accommodation at posting location, CGHS-equivalent state medical coverage, and pension benefits. MP's cost of living is lower than metros - this salary provides an upper-middle-class lifestyle even in Bhopal (state capital).

Initial postings: SDM (Sub-Divisional Magistrate) manages land revenue, law and order, development schemes, election duties, and public grievances across a sub-division. DSP (Deputy Superintendent of Police) leads police operations in a sub-division covering multiple police stations.

BDO manages rural development programs at block level - MGNREGA, housing schemes, agricultural programs. MP-specific governance challenges: Managing tiger reserves (Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench, Panna - MP has the highest tiger population among all states), tribal welfare in Schedule V areas (PESA Act implementation, FRA 2006), diamond mining regulation in Panna, Narmada valley development projects, and flood management along Chambal and Narmada rivers.

Promotion path: SDM/DSP/BDO → ADM (5-7 years) → Collector/SP (12-15 years) → Divisional Commissioner/DIG (20+ years) → Principal Secretary/Additional Chief Secretary. The Collector of Indore administers India's cleanest city (Swachh Survekshan winner 7 consecutive years) - arguably the most prestigious collector posting in India.

extra_sections.heading: MPPSC vs UPSC - strategic comparison for MP aspirants
content: Syllabus overlap: 75% of MPPSC GS is identical to UPSC GS. The additional 25% is MP-specific content that UPSC doesn't test.

Preparing for both simultaneously is highly efficient - your UPSC preparation directly helps MPPSC, and the MP GK preparation adds manageable additional study. Unique MPPSC features that differ from UPSC: Ethics paper is 200 marks (UPSC: 250), Hindi Essay is a separate 100-mark paper (UPSC has essay as GS paper), and Interview carries 175 marks (UPSC: 275).
The higher relative Interview weightage in MPPSC means personality and communication skills matter more. Competition: UPSC - 10 lakh for 1,000 posts.
MPPSC - 4-6 lakh for 200-500 posts. Per-vacancy competition is similar.

But MPPSC's MP GK advantage means candidates with deep state knowledge can overcome general knowledge gaps. This specialization advantage doesn't exist in UPSC where all candidates study the same national syllabus.
Career advantage of MPPSC: Guaranteed home state posting. MP is India's second-largest state - diverse geography, tribal regions, tiger reserves, historical sites, and industrial centers.

An MPPSC officer serves in dramatically different environments - from tribal Bastar to cosmopolitan Indore, from forested Pachmarhi to agricultural Malwa. This diversity within one state is unmatched.

extra_sections.heading: MPPSC interview - 175 marks that change ranks
content: MPPSC Interview carries 175 marks - the highest interview weightage among major state PSCs (BPSC: 120, RPSC: 100, JPSC: 100). This means a strong interview performance can catapult you 50-100 ranks upward, while a weak interview can drop you from a selected position to the waiting list.
Interview preparation is not optional - it's a strategic necessity. Interview format: 30-45 minutes with a panel of 3-5 members.

Conducted primarily in Hindi but English is acceptable. Questions cover: personal introduction and background, your district's history-geography-problems, MP current affairs and government policies, national issues and governance, and situational questions testing administrative aptitude.

Guaranteed interview questions: 'Tell us about yourself' (prepare a crisp 2-minute intro), 'Tell us about your district' (know population, literacy, major crops, industries, tourist sites, and 3 key development challenges), 'Why civil services?' (give a specific answer rooted in MP context, not generic motivation), 'What would you do as SDM in a flood-affected area?' (demonstrate practical administrative thinking). Scoring well in interview: Be genuine - the panel has years of experience spotting rehearsed answers.
Show awareness of ground realities in MP, not just textbook knowledge. If you don't know an answer, say so honestly rather than bluffing.

Maintain eye contact, sit upright, speak clearly in Hindi, and show confidence without arrogance. Practice mock interviews with friends or at coaching institutes - raw intelligence without interview practice loses 20-30 marks.

extra_sections.text: Madhya Pradesh is India's second-largest state with tiger reserves, tribal regions, diamond mines, and the cleanest city. An MPPSC officer managing this diversity - from Khajuraho's heritage to Indore's smart city initiatives - experiences governance at its most varied and rewarding. Home state posting, diverse challenges, and direct impact on 8 crore lives.

extra_sections.heading: Books and resources for MPPSC
content: MP GK: 'Madhya Pradesh Samanya Gyan' by Arihant (comprehensive), 'MP Ek Parichay' by McGraw Hill, 'Madhya Pradesh Ka Sampoorna Bhugol' for geography, and 'MP Ka Itihas' by Punekar publications. These cover MP history, geography, economy, art, culture, and governance comprehensively.

Standard GS: NCERT Class 6-12 (foundation), Spectrum Modern India, Laxmikanth Indian Polity, Shankar IAS Environment, Ramesh Singh Indian Economy. These are the same books used for UPSC - the 75% syllabus overlap means your investment in these books serves dual purpose.

Current affairs: Dainik Bhaskar (best MP coverage in Hindi), Navduniya (MP-specific daily), Pratiyogita Darpan (monthly compilation). For MP government schemes: check mp.gov.in regularly for new scheme announcements, budget highlights, and policy updates.

The CM's Twitter/social media handles are good sources for scheme launches. Coaching in MP: Sharma Academy Indore (most popular for MPPSC), Kautilya Academy Bhopal, Bansal Academy Bhopal, and online coaching from Drishti IAS (Hindi medium, covers both UPSC and MPPSC).
Fees: Rs 25,000-70,000 for 6-12 month programs. Indore and Bhopal are the two main coaching hubs.
Online options: Rs 8,000-20,000 from the same institutes.

extra_sections.heading: Official resources and helpline
content: MPPSC official portal: mppsc.mp.gov.in - notifications, admit cards, results, and previous year papers. Registration portal: mppsc.nic.in for online application.
Helpline: 0755-2763885 (MPPSC office, Indore Road, Bhopal). For exam-related queries, email at the address given in the notification.
Previous year papers: Available free at mppsc.mp.gov.in under 'Question Papers' section. Solve papers from 2010-2025 for both Prelims and Mains.

MPPSC has predictable topic patterns - certain MP history topics, geography features, and constitutional provisions appear every cycle. Analyzing 10 years of papers reveals the 20-25 high-frequency topics that account for 50% of Prelims marks.

MPPSC has revised schedules mid-cycle before, including for the 2025 batch. Always confirm against mppsc.mp.gov.in before booking travel or accommodation.

preparation_tips: MPPSC Prelims GS paper tests factual knowledge more than conceptual frameworks. Focus on facts: exact numbers (MP population, literacy rate, forest cover %), major production figures (soybean tons/year), geographical coordinates, historical dates. Read standard GS books (Lucent, Manorama Yearbook) + MP-specific materials (Sanjeev Verma's MP GK, government yearbooks).

Hindi language proficiency is scoring in MPPSC Mains. Both Hindi language paper and Hindi essay carry significant marks. Most MP candidates are comfortable in Hindi - use this advantage. Write practice essays in Hindi weekly from month 4. If Hindi is weak, dedicate 3 months to Hindi grammar, comprehension, and essay writing.

MPPSC conducts exams at irregular intervals - sometimes 2 exams in one year, sometimes gaps. Stay prepared year-round rather than targeting specific dates. If you miss this 2026 notification, another might come within 6-12 months. Keep revision ongoing.

Join MPPSC-specific coaching if possible. Bhopal and Indore centers (like Sanjeev Verma's institute, other local coaching) offer MP GK modules. For self-study, follow: mppsc.com for notifications, Sanjeev Verma sir's YouTube channel for MP GK, join MPPSC Telegram groups for peer discussions and current affairs sharing.

Solve previous year MPPSC papers (2015-2025, 10 years) multiple times. Question patterns repeat. Some exact questions appear across years with slight variations. After 3-4 complete revisions of previous papers, you'll recognize 15-20% of actual exam questions.

faqs.question: MPPSC vs UPPSC - which is easier and which to choose?
faqs.answer:
Vacancy-wise: MPPSC (155-500 seats) vs UPPSC (200-400 seats) similar. Competition per seat: Similar (4L+ applicants).

Difficulty-wise: Similar. Question patterns: MPPSC more factual, UPPSC more conceptual.

Choose based on: If Madhya Pradesh home state, choose MPPSC (advantage in MP GK). If Uttar Pradesh home state, choose UPPSC.

Both are equally achievable. Many candidates from one state appear for both.

faqs.question: Can non-MP residents apply for MPPSC?
faqs.answer:
Yes. MPPSC is open to all Indian citizens.

No domicile requirement for most general category posts. Some specific reserved category posts may require MP domicile - check detailed notification.

General category applicants from any state can compete.

faqs.question: DSP vs Naib Tehsildar - which is better?
faqs.answer:
DSP: Level 10 (higher pay), dynamic police work, field duty, transfers frequent, law enforcement pressure. Naib Tehsildar: Level 8 (lower pay), land revenue administration, office-based initially, less physical risk, powerful role in property disputes.

DSP offers more action and career advancement; Naib Tehsildar offers stability. Choose: Enjoy field policing?

→ DSP. Prefer revenue/administrative work?

→ Naib Tehsildar.

faqs.question: What's the difference between MPPSC Prelims Paper 1 and Paper 2 strategy?
faqs.answer:
Paper 1 (GS): Counts for ranking. With new 3-mark negative marking, only attempt 50-70 questions accurately (achieving 45-60 marks out of 300).

Don't attempt all 100. Strategy: Solve questions you're 90%+ confident about.

Skip medium-confidence questions. Attempt guesses only on 5-10 questions maximum.

Paper 2 (CSAT): Qualifying only (need 33%). Less important.

Quick strategy: Solve easy math (30%), easy reasoning (30%), English (30%), skip hard questions. Your Paper 2 score doesn't affect ranking - just crossing 33% suffices.

Many toppers score 50-60 in Paper 2 and still get selected because Paper 1 performance is dominant.

faqs.question: How frequent are MPPSC exams? Should I keep applying until selected?
faqs.answer:
MPPSC exam frequency is irregular - not annual. Last major notification was January 2026 (155 vacancies for SSE).

Before this, exams happened in 2019, 2022 - so roughly 2-3 year gaps. Strategy: Don't wait for next MPPSC notification if it's 2+ years away.

Keep preparing and simultaneously apply for other state PSCs: UPPSC, BPSC, if you're in Hindi heartland. Or pursue UPSC CSE parallel.

Also prepare for SSC exams (CGL, CHSL) which have more frequent notifications. Having multiple exam options ensures you eventually get a government job.

MPPSC selection is not mandatory - good performance in UPPSC or other PSC is equally valuable.

faqs.question: What is the MPPSC age limit?
faqs.answer:
General: 21-40 years. SC/ST from MP: 21-45 years.

OBC from MP: 21-43 years. PwD: 21-45 years.

These are among the most generous age limits for any state PSC exam - giving candidates up to 20 attempts (annual exam) within the eligible age range.

faqs.question: Is MPPSC conducted in Hindi or English?
faqs.answer:
Both Hindi and English options are available. Prelims question papers are bilingual (Hindi + English).

Mains answers can be written in Hindi or English - your choice. Interview is primarily in Hindi but English is accepted.

Most MP candidates write in Hindi - evaluators are comfortable with both languages.

faqs.question: How many vacancies does MPPSC announce?
faqs.answer:
MPPSC State Service Exam typically announces 200-500 vacancies per cycle across MPAS, MPPS, and allied services. Some exceptional cycles have seen 700+ vacancies.

The exact number is in the notification at mppsc.mp.gov.in. Vacancies are distributed across services based on pending positions.

faqs.question: What is the full form of MPPSC?
faqs.answer: MPPSC stands for Madhya Pradesh Public Service Commission. It conducts the State Service Examination (Rajya Seva), the main route to MP administrative and police posts like Deputy Collector and DSP.

faqs.question: What is the salary of an MPPSC Deputy Collector?
faqs.answer: A Deputy Collector (SDM) sits at Pay Level 10 with a basic of ₹56,100. Entry in-hand is roughly ₹75,000 to ₹90,000 a month after allowances, rising with service and promotions.

faqs.question: Is there negative marking in MPPSC Prelims 2026?
faqs.answer:
For 2026, MPPSC introduced negative marking in Paper 1 (GS): 3 marks for a correct answer and 1 mark deducted for a wrong one. Paper 2 (CSAT) is qualifying.

Some older guides still show the no-negative-marking pattern, so confirm from the official notification at mppsc.mp.gov.in.

faqs.question: MPPSC Mains admit card 2026 kab aayega?
faqs.answer:
Expect it from the last week of August 2026 on mppsc.mp.gov.in, roughly two weeks before the exam. Download it with your registration number and date of birth.

Check the paper-wise dates, shift timings and centre address as soon as it opens. Report any name, photo or signature discrepancy to the commission immediately.

faqs.question: When was the MPPSC Prelims result 2026 declared?
faqs.answer:
The Prelims result was declared on 22 May 2026, publishing the roll numbers of candidates shortlisted for Mains across 155 State and Forest Service posts.

The answer key had come earlier, on 27 April 2026, a day after the 26 April exam. Cut-off marks are released separately by category.

faqs.question: Is MPPSC Forest Service Mains on the same date?
faqs.answer:
No. State Service Mains runs 7 to 12 September 2026, while State Forest Service Mains is on 27 September 2026.

They are separate exams with separate Prelims result lists. Check which list carries your roll number before planning around either date.

faqs.question: What happened to the MPPSC 2025 cycle Mains?
faqs.answer:
The 2025 cycle is still in progress alongside the 2026 one, and its Mains schedule has been revised more than once.

Because the dates have moved, confirm the current position directly on mppsc.mp.gov.in rather than trusting older articles or forwarded messages.

faqs.question: MPPSC 2027 notification kab aayegi?
faqs.answer:
MPPSC has recently issued its State Service notification around the end of the calendar year, with the 2026 one released on 31 December 2025.

The commission publishes an annual exam calendar in December that fixes the following year's dates. Watch mppsc.mp.gov.in from around November for the calendar and the notification.
